decisions.reason: As an adjustable cardboard quarter-pallet display, it builds directly on the firm's core design and paper-display know-how, so management is likely to retain and refine it rather than exit.

The pegboard-back cardboard shelf display is still close to the firm's established display competencies, and a large firm with in-house development can learn from early market use and improve the format.

This is a straightforward cardboard quarter-pallet display in the firm's core product space, making it highly compatible with existing production, customer relationships, and incremental innovation routines.
An eighth-pallet cardboard display is a nearby extension of the firm's existing retail-display knowledge base, so absorptive capacity arguments favor keeping it in the assortment.
A wooden display pallet is materially less related to the firm's paper-based knowledge base and manufacturing strengths, so management is more likely to reallocate resources away from it.

Although the media-products niche may be narrower, the product remains a cardboard quarter-pallet display and therefore can be supported by the firm's existing capabilities and customer-learning processes.
